newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond market shows indigestion on pfds.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond market shows indigestion on pfds.

text.p: U.S. junk bond investors began to show the first signs of indigestion on Tuesday with the large quantity of exchangeable preferred stock offerings to hit the U.S. high-yield corporate bond market in recent weeks, traders and analysts said.

An exchangeable preferred stock offering by Granite Broadcasting Corp, priced at 12 3/4 percent on Tuesday. That level was 25 basis points higher than price talk which was between 12 1/4 percent and 12 1/2 percent.
Goldman Sachs & Co, the underwriter did immediately return calls.
Market sources said Goldman syndicate officials struggled to fill orders for the deal because many junk investors had already filled up on similar offerings.
Seeking to tap strong investor demand for high yield/high risk paper, media and broadcasting companies have issued around $1 billion of these securities in recent weeks.
Analysts said the securities offer juicy yields becuase they pay-in-kind for the first several years and are generally issued by highly leveraged companies.
"There is a small and relatively short window for getting these deals done," an analyst said.
"Granite came close to missing it."

While recent preferred deals have all traded higher immediately after being priced, traders said the Granite preferreds, which were priced at par, were quoted as low at 99 1/8 in the aftermarket on Tuesday.
Traders noted prices on other exchangeable preferred stocks in the secondary market were also lower on Tuesday.
Granite Broadcasting is a New York-based television broadcasting company.
In the broader junk market, traders said new issues were the main focus of investor attention.
Premier Parks, an amusement park company, sold $125 million in B2/B-plus rated senior notes due '02 via Lehman Brothers Inc. The bonds were quoted at 102 3/8 following the offering.
Late on Tuesday, Orion Network Systems, an international satellite communications concern, sold $445 million in 10-year senior notes and $265 million in zero coupon bonds via Morgan Stanley & Co Inc.
Traders said focus on new issues helped push junk bonds prices higher by 1/8 to 1/4 of a point in the broader market.
In the high-grade market, ITT Corp bonds were the big movers, ending the day roughly 10 basis points wider.
The spread widening occurred as a result of Hilton Hotels Corp's announcement on Monday night of a hostile bid for ITT.
Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's put Hilton and ITT debt on watch for a ratings downgrade soon after.
Despite the price drop, traders said few ITT bonds actually traded, as investors were waiting to see whether Hilton would alter its bid.
In the new issue market for high-grade debt, Wachovia Corp sold $300 million in floating-rate trust preferred securities via a Merrill Lynch & Co-led syndicate.
